newsitem.title: USA: WAPA cuts power sales from US West hydro project.
newsitem.headline: WAPA cuts power sales from US West hydro project.

text.p: The Western Area Power Administration (WAPA) said Monday it will reduce electricity sales from the Salt Lake Integrated Project, reflecting the lower snowpack levels measured at the facility.
"We're reducing schedules effective tomorrow," said a spokeswoman for the federal power marketing agency.

Because snowpack readings in the upper Colorado River Basin on March 1 fell from month-ago level, Bureau of Reclamation (BuRec) decided to cut the water flow to conserve resources for fish and generation requirements later this spring, she said.
BuRec planned to trim flows into Salt Lake hydro project by 3,000 cubic feet per second (cfs) to 24,000 cfs, she added.
The spokeswoman could not provide the exact amount of energy cut to all WAPA customers who buy power from the Salt Lake complex, but noted "It will not be a big reduction in generation."
The power reduction at Salt Lake project would remain in effect at least through the end of the month until the next snowpack report, she said.
BuRec owns and operates the 1,855 megawatt (MW) Salt Lake project whose biggest generating facility is the eight-unit, 1,356 MW Glen Canyon hydro plant on the Arizona/Utah border.
WAPA markets the output from the hydroelectric complex to 132 customers in Arizona, Colorado, California, Utah, New Mexico, and Wyoming.

Market talk on the flow cut today helped boost spot electricity prices in the Northwest. At the California-Oregon Border (COB), day-ahead power for firm, peak delivery rose to $14.00-15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), 50 cents to a dollar higher than Friday.
